key_insight: This paper shows that small multimodal GUI agents can improve task planning by learning from their own autonomous exploration and by reusing successful and failed experiences. The result is better decomposition of repetitive GUI tasks and stronger generalization across websites.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the weak planning ability and poor cross-website generalization of small open-source MLLM-based GUI agents, which limits their usefulness for complex web task execution.
method: Introduce Planning Experience Exploration and Utilization (PEEU), a framework for collecting planning experience autonomously.
Explore GUI environments to generate task-planning experiences without relying heavily on expensive human annotations.
Use hindsight experience utilization to learn from both successful and unsuccessful attempts, improving future planning decisions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical path to make lightweight, privacy-preserving GUI agents more reliable on real-world web tasks. It reduces dependence on large proprietary models while improving planning quality and transferability.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing autonomous exploration -> experience storage -> hindsight utilization -> improved planning
Before/after comparison chart of task planning performance across websites
Icon set for GUI actions, exploration, memory, and planning
Flowchart illustrating how successful and failed attempts are reused for learning
paper_title: Empowering GUI Agents via Autonomous Experience Exploration and Hindsight Experience Utilization for Task Planning
paper_authors: Tianyi Men, Zhuoran Jin, Pengfei Cao, Yubo Chen, Kang Liu
